seed_version_description: 56-word account; controlled masculine on ðǣm sǣ in example1; final account has no narrative nū.
independent_translation: Two men were on the shore. They had five animals. The first man said: ‘If you help me, we can bind the animals.’ The second man said: ‘I will help you. Let us bind the animals.’ They bound the animals, and the first man gave his companion food. The animals were bound, and the men had food.
interpretation_notes: Helpe is second-singular present subjunctive in the contingent request, although its spelling also occurs elsewhere in a first-singular indicative cell.
Magon is first-plural present indicative of ability; the conditional use does not force a subjunctive into the main clause.
Wille expresses the second man's willing intention, naturally a promise here; this is not an independently taught generic future tense.
Binden with wē is a first-plural exhortation, not a second-person imperative.
His gefēran is the recipient of the food, in the dative. The story makes the second man the companion, while his itself is not an intrinsically reflexive pronoun.
Final bunden is an uninflected verbal passive participle; the text does not require the animals to be an attributive adjective target.
